rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_codex/ids/candidates.py hides retrieval, batched judgment and routing behind retrieve_candidates/route_ids/judge_candidates/route and three frozen dataclasses (479 lines), and §8 concentrates every SignalSource→IMASNode edge write, delete, reader and route count in graph_ops.py behind that module's gc-threaded functions.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan's MAPS_TO_IMAS census matches the tree exactly (three MATCH-gated writers at imas_codex/ids/models.py:580, imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:367, imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:2008 and the one delete at imas_codex/cli/map.py:661), and §8 consolidates all four into graph_ops.py beside write_candidates/clear_candidates, moving count_candidates_by_route to the same owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 adds no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family (its new refusals reuse the existing CandidateWriteError) and names what it retires: --skip-metadata, --skip-errors, count_sources_by_mapping_status, and the SignalSource fields mapping_target_path and mapping_target_ids.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites and extends the right mechanisms (hybrid_dd_search, call_decisions in discovery/base/llm.py, claims.py claim_batch/has_pending, PipelineCost, graph_ops.py), but §8's uniqueness claim for the per-source wiki/code bridge omits the existing per-source code reader fetch_source_code_refs.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the §8 additions read_candidates and select_candidate are not wrappers over write_candidates: select_candidate is justified in the plan's own text (a pick must flag one existing edge, while write_candidates deletes and rewrites a source's whole shortlist), and workers.py's claim helpers delegate to claims.py by the pattern §7 already established.
